# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 10:07 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 161 active entries of tips_notebook.json (18 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a track can't tell protection from framing or the Katana. But if a trusted Lookout names X as the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 11 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads and explain any switch before the vote. A read/vote mismatch is only a lead: never shoot or hang on it alone. (seen in 9 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat unless a full census proves otherwise, and the Katana holder reads Good that night. (seen in 8 games)
- Unless a Clerk may have an unused rig, treat nomination and trial as separate votes. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) needs a test, not an automatic acquittal. (seen in 10 games)
- Put every result, and tonight's labeled plan, in your will each Day. Post results that matter publicly too, since a Mortician can hide wills. (seen in 6 games)

## Village
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. Players who DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new info are a likely Yakuza bloc. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No or Innocent with them, argued to delay, or exchanged PMs with them. A Guilty vote clears nobody, since it may be a bus. Demand a claim before hanging. (seen in 11 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name another living player's exact role; say 'ask X'. (seen in 11 games)
- Never announce tonight's investigation or protection target, publicly or by PM. It tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 7 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, do slot math daily. A claim that duplicates a role listed once, or that overflows the unseen slots, marks a liar, and a late lone Vanilla is often the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 4 games)
- If a trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among that side's voters. Recompute the threshold, then pick out the stuffer by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty). If your Innocents plus a Ballot Stuffer can save them, defend them. Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later. (seen in 14 games)
- Fake roles whose tokens match yours (an Accountant may audit you), and never a role a living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict. Don't switch claims once broken. (seen in 11 games)
- Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game. (seen in 8 games)
- Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit. Avoid hitting confident unclaimed organizers, who may be alerting Veterans. (seen in 7 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retry, or hang the defended Neutral. (seen in 8 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder and target every night; with two left, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout could have seen. Agree a cover in night chat and admit the visit at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Feed exact-role info (Diviner, Mortician, claims) into Ritualist guesses for certain kills, alongside the Katana. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked; nobody else knows the target. If you must explain, pick one claim and never switch. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 6 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat. (seen in 11 games)

## Eavesdropper
- Pick a target who will survive and send PMs, such as the Day 1 PM-cluster starter. An empty record clears nobody. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard vocal analysts and claimed investigators. Once you're claimed, spend a token to self-protect instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 10 games)
- You get no save feedback; say only that a survival is consistent with your protection. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check on an unverifiable claim, flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners), never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; every waiting night lets the town hang you first. (seen in 3 games)

task:
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken; the resolutions looked rule-consistent. Minor items: Heidi's N3 report said 'got no reading' for a self-pick, which is fine but undocumented. Carol publicly claimed 'Pharmacist died N1, so only a real Party Animal could block'. That was a player reasoning error (roles can repeat), not a bug, though the ledger could remind players of it.
answers.suggestions: Add a short Yakuza dawn chat or let teammates' private results appear in the night report. Allow last-will edits during your own night turn. In the ledger, flag that roles can repeat unless a census proves otherwise. Consider letting dead players see a brief per-day summary, which they already effectively get.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) The Diviner's self-pick: R6 lets a role target itself unless it says otherwise, and the Diviner text says a Yakuza pick gets Strong Defense. So a Diviner can quietly give itself Strong Defense every night. That matters a lot for a Vigilante choosing Basic vs Strong shots, but you only see it by combining two rules. 2) The Vigilante text doesn't say how the shot is revealed. Presumably the cause shows as 'Vigilante' and the shooter gets success feedback, but it's not spelled out whether a Cardinal misfire after my shot is shown as a separate cause. 3) R14's stall clock counts Days and Nights separately, which made it hard to tell when a no-kill night actually started to matter.
answers.missing_information: 1) A running per-night summary of who claimed to visit whom. I had to rebuild Ivan's and Judy's visit logs from scattered messages. 2) My own budget history across Days, and how much carried over. 3) Which roles are possible in this setup. Without any role list, deciding whether Ivan could be a second Pharmacist was pure guesswork.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to confirm privately to one trusted player (Carol or Grace) that I'm the Vigilante without everyone seeing a PM ping. The public PM-sender visibility makes this almost impossible without painting a target. That's by design, but it pushed me to stay silent instead.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken. Small oddity: Heidi's N4 result says 'your Diviner action did nothing'. A Yakuza self-pick has no visit, so whether a block stops a self-protection is fine by R9, but it's worth confirming that is intended. Also, the ledger listed Carol's N3 audit claim as 'fits Village role', which leaked partial info about my tokens. That's player behavior, not a bug.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add a 'claimed night actions' table to the public ledger: player, night, claimed target. 2) Show each player's carried-over budget at the start of each Day. 3) State explicitly in the Diviner text whether self-targeting gives Strong Defense, since it changes how a Vigilante should size shots. 4) Allow a slightly longer notepad for long games.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Puppeteer plus R21: my Night 2 puppet on Judy should lapse because I died that night to the Jester's revenge. It isn't clear whether Judy was still told she was puppeted or silenced for Day 3. Day 3 shows Judy speaking normally, so it lapsed, but the rules don't say what the puppet target is told when that happens. 2) Puppeteer text: 'they can't chat or see private messages... they still nominate, vote' doesn't say who answers trial-defense turns if the puppet is nominated, or whether the puppet sees its own public messages. 3) Diviner self-pick: it took a careful read to see that picking yourself gives Strong Defense and no reading.
answers.missing_information: 1) The Yakuza night report gives only the actions teammates chose, not their results. So I never learned Heidi's Night 2 divine (Trapper drawn on Judy's group) before Day 3. That made the planned puppet script, a soft claim that avoids clashing with the divine, guesswork. 2) It was hard to track which Yakuza covers were already used (three Vanilla claims). A per-faction summary of claimed covers in night chat would help.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) There's no Yakuza chat window between the night results and the start of Day. Heidi had to invent a signal-word scheme ('curious'/'careful') to pass her divine result to me through public speech, and a puppeteer acting at Day start would need that result immediately. 2) I wanted to know whether the Jester's revenge was a risk to me in particular; it was pure chance, which is fine, but nothing could be planned around it.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Formats are inconsistent: Night 1 results use 'Moderator (private): You ...', while Night 3/4 use 'Night 3: ...' prefixes, and Erin's N4 result reads 'Your guess was wrong: Heidi is not a Grunt' instead of the earlier wording. Not harmful, but inconsistent. 2) Otherwise everything matched the rules as I read them: the Katana passed to Heidi after Mallory's death, the puppet lapsed after my death, and the block stopped the N4 Katana attack.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add a short Yakuza dawn chat, or include teammates' private results (divine draws, audits) in the Yakuza night report. 2) State explicitly in the Puppeteer text what happens to the puppet if the Puppeteer dies at night (lapses, and whether the target is told). 3) Standardize moderator result wording across nights. 4) Consider a reminder in the Yakuza prompt of cover claims already used by teammates, so three members don't all default to Vanilla.

answers.confusing_rules: Mostly clear. Two small ambiguities. First, whether a Puppeteer's puppet lapses if the Puppeteer dies that same night. R21 implies it does, but the Puppeteer entry itself doesn't say so. Second, the Oracle has no limit on guesses and leaves no visit trace. As a Serial Killer hiding behind a Vanilla claim, I had no counterplay once an Oracle guessed my exact role, and nothing in the rules hinted at how strong that is against Neutral killers.
answers.missing_information: As the Serial Killer I only learn success or failure. I couldn't tell whether a kill would have happened anyway: on N3 Alice was also hit by the Katana, so my kill was redundant and gained me nothing. A note like 'target was also attacked by another source' would have helped me plan. I also had to track claims and flips by hand to work out which unclaimed players were safe to kill. The ledger helped a lot with that.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: On my trial I wanted to propose a conditional test (Sheriff checks Erin tonight) that the town could commit to. There's no way to make binding agreements, which is fine, but the trial format gave me only two short messages against eight confirming Guilty posts.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None that broke the rules. Night results looked consistent: Mallory was role-blocked and still killed by my Strong attack; Heidi's Diviner self-pick gave her Strong Defense and no reading; Bob's Jester revenge hit Peggy, who voted Guilty. The phrasing of moderator results varied in style between nights (e.g. 'Your attack on Niaj succeeded' vs 'Night 2 result: ...'), which is cosmetic.
answers.suggestions: 1) Consider capping or token-limiting Oracle guesses, or making a correct Oracle hit on a Neutral killer less instantly decisive. A 15-player game with a nightly free exact-role guess makes a hidden SK very fragile. 2) Tell killers when their target died to multiple attacks, so redundant kills are visible. 3) In the claims ledger, flag claims that contradict a flip, such as a dead player whose will said Vanilla but who flipped a power role.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) R9 conflicts with itself for players with no night action. It says 'Role-blocked players are told they were role-blocked' and also 'blocking a player who has no night action has no effect.' Bob (Jester) was blocked by both Ivan and Niaj on N1. I read 'no effect' as 'no notice' and told him nothing, but either reading fits the text. The difference matters: a block notice is public-facing information that Bob could have used. 2) R21 says the Puppeteer's effect lapses if the user dies, but not whether the puppet target is still told they're puppeted. Peggy puppeted Judy on N2 and died the same night to Jester revenge. I let it lapse silently, so Judy chatted normally on Day 3 and was never told. I had to infer that. 3) The Diviner targeting themself isn't explicitly covered. Heidi picked herself on N3 and N4. I applied 'If they are Yakuza, Strong Defense, no reading.' A line confirming that self-target is legal, and whether it counts as a self-visit for the Fortune Teller, would help. 4) R19 on the Katana holder: on N4 Heidi was role-blocked but still held the Katana. I ruled she read Not Evil to Grace, because she held it at the end of the night even though her actions were blocked. The text supports this, but it isn't stated explicitly for blocked holders.
answers.missing_information: 1) There was no visible seat-order list. The Day 1 transcript shows Grace, Judy and Olivia speaking after Carol, because they passed in round 1. That makes the seat order look non-alphabetical. I had to reconstruct the circle (alphabetical) to check the Diviner groups Bob/Carol/Dave and Ivan/Judy/Mallory. 2) There was no persistent state panel for: trap location and armed status (Judy's trap moved Dave to Grace and stayed there through N3 and N4 because she took no action), pending Day effects (puppet, rig) and whether they lapsed, Katana holder history, and token counts per player. I tracked all of these by hand. 3) The Jester revenge needed the Guilty-voter list filtered to players alive at the start of the night. That list wasn't given to me automatically.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to send Peggy a clear 'you were attacked by the Jester's revenge and died' notice. Her N2 result only covered the puppet token, because the revenge isn't a player action in my action list. I also wanted to tell Judy at dawn on Day 3 that a puppet had lapsed, or to explicitly rule that she shouldn't be told, but I had no defined message to use. And I wanted a way to log a ruling such as the R9 no-notice decision so it would show in the game record.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) My death notifications were inconsistent. Dave (N1) got 'You were attacked with the Katana' and Niaj got 'You were attacked by a Serial Killer', with no 'and you died'. Mallory (N2) and Alice (N3) were told 'and you died'. 2) Peggy, killed by the Jester's revenge on N2, was never notified of the attack, which R3/R20 step 5 says she should be. 3) The N2 Yakuza report went to Heidi and Peggy even though Peggy died that night. It's harmless, but odd. 4) Mechanically everything else checked out: the Sheriff read Jester as Evil, the trap was not armed on the night it was placed, Mallory's N2 Katana attack was stopped by Ivan's block, and the Katana passed to Heidi. Alice's double fatal cause was revealed, the nomination thresholds were correct, and the Village win was checked correctly after Heidi's hanging, with the Jester Bob also winning.
answers.suggestions: 1) Rewrite R9 to say plainly whether players with no night action are told they were role-blocked. My recommendation: they are not told. 2) Add to R21 that a lapsed puppet is never announced to its target. 3) Have the program generate attack and death notices automatically for non-action sources (Jester/Executioner revenge, Cardinal), and standardize wording to 'attacked by X; you survived/died'. 4) Show the seat circle at the start of each Day and in the moderator view. 5) Give the moderator a state dashboard: tokens, trap positions and armed status, Katana holder, pending next-Day effects and their lapse status, and Guilty voters eligible for revenge. 6) Explicitly allow self-targeting for the Diviner and say how it interacts with the Fortune Teller count. 7) Add a 'ruling log' that is saved with the game.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Traps arm only from the next night, so put the trap on someone the Katana is likely to hit in two nights' time: a vocal investigator or analyst. Re-target every night rather than leaving it parked. A trap on an already-claimed Sheriff is predictable, and a lone Katana holder simply avoids that player.

If a Lookout reveals that you visited the Katana victim, claim at once with mechanics others can verify (token count for the Accountant, alignment check). A clean claim that fits the audits ended the suspicion within one round.

A night with no Katana kill that lines up with a confirmed blocker's target is strong evidence, especially once a third party has confirmed one of that blocker's past blocks. Once the Pharmacist has flipped, a confirmed block also points to a real Party Animal.
Late lone 'Vanilla' claims from long-quiet players are prime suspects for the last Yakuza. Their claims are unverifiable, and a Diviner or Grunt carrying the Katana reads Not Evil anyway.
Short one-line speeches on Days 1-2 save budget for trial days, when you need to claim, cross-check, and state a conditional plan such as 'if X flips Village, hang Y next'.

tips_feedback.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates.
tips_feedback.why: The only Day 1 PM pair (Bob-Niaj) gave the town its first lead. It turned out to be a Jester fishing a Pharmacist, but it still produced an early flip.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester...
tips_feedback.why: We hanged Bob on a Sheriff Evil check without weighing that a Jester also reads Evil. The Jester revenge then killed a random Guilty voter (it happened to hit Peggy, a Yakuza, so we got lucky).

tips_feedback.tip: Unclaimed players, stay unclaimed / Don't hint at a power role on Day 1
tips_feedback.why: Olivia (Vigilante) stayed hidden and survived. Withholding role names kept the Katana focused on known investigators.

tips_feedback.tip: A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's block log, confirmed by Olivia's N3 block, made the block/no-kill pattern trustworthy and led to the correct Heidi hang.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's Not Evil on Heidi was correctly discounted, so the town didn't clear the actual Katana holder.

lessons.tip: Once the Neutral killers are dead, a lone surviving Yakuza holder is checkable through a confirmed blocker. Block/no-kill nights matched against a third party's independent confirmation of a block (e.g. the blocked player saying so) form a real mechanical lead. Use it rather than waiting.

As Cardinal, claim Vanilla publicly but put the true Cardinal claim in your will. If you die, the town won't misread the random Good death as a Katana kill, and the Yakuza get no reason to target you deliberately. Reveal publicly only when facing a hang, since hanging a Cardinal costs the Village two players.

When a claimant names a hidden Neutral with an exact-role hit (Oracle), hang the named player at once. A last Yakuza can't know who the SK is, so the claim tests itself on the flip. Arguments like 'test the claimant first' just buy the killer another night.

Before you treat an attack on yourself as proof of innocence, check whether your role reads Good to alignment checks while holding the Katana. Late in the game, Not Evil results clear nobody, so weigh claim timing and late Vanilla claims above Sheriff results.
Short Day 1 agreement messages followed by silence are enough. Save your budget for the day results start flowing, when you'll need to question claimants and do vote math.

lessons.tip: Block the player you suspect of holding the Katana, not just a probable investigator. A no-kill night that lines up with your block is the strongest mechanical lead the town gets against a lone last Yakuza, since Sheriff checks read the holder as Not Evil.

Write your exact block target in your will and post it publicly the Day after, before anyone can confirm it. A target who later confirms they were blocked (e.g. Olivia saying she was role-blocked N3) proves you are a real blocker. That makes later block/no-kill matches credible enough to hang on.

Before a hang on a single unverifiable log, commit publicly to 'if they flip Village, I'm next.' It costs little when you are honest and gets the town to accept the vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the mechanics before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat unless a full census proves otherwise, and the Katana holder reads Good that night.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's 'Ivan could be a second Pharmacist' and 'the holder skipped on purpose' arguments were mechanically possible. The town weighed them correctly against the verified N3 block instead of dismissing them.

tips_feedback.why: This was hurt for the Yakuza: the only Day 1 PM was Bob to Niaj, and Niaj's Pharmacist flip made Bob, the Jester, look Yakuza. Even a PM from a non-teammate became a public anchor. Here it misled the town into hanging the Jester, whose revenge happened to kill a Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: Nobody applied it. Bob's 'mild dissent' pressure-nomination push on Day 1 was a Jester tell, yet he was hanged 13-0, so every voter was exposed to the revenge. Luckily it hit Peggy, a Yakuza, but it could easily have killed a key town role.

lessons.tip: Traps arm only from the next night, so put the trap on someone the Katana is likely to hit in two nights' time: a vocal investigator or analyst. Re-target every night rather than leaving it parked. A trap on an already-claimed Sheriff is predictable, and a lone Katana holder simply avoids that player.

If a Lookout reveals that you visited the Katana victim, claim at once with mechanics others can verify (token count for the Accountant, alignment check). A clean claim that fits the audits ended the suspicion within one round.

A night with no Katana kill that lines up with a confirmed blocker's target is strong evidence, especially once a third party has confirmed one of that blocker's past blocks. Once the Pharmacist has flipped, a confirmed block also points to a real Party Animal.
Late lone 'Vanilla' claims from long-quiet players are prime suspects for the last Yakuza. Their claims are unverifiable, and a Diviner or Grunt carrying the Katana reads Not Evil anyway.
Short one-line speeches on Days 1-2 save budget for trial days, when you need to claim, cross-check, and state a conditional plan such as 'if X flips Village, hang Y next'.

tips_feedback.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates.
tips_feedback.why: The only Day 1 PM pair (Bob-Niaj) gave the town its first lead. It turned out to be a Jester fishing a Pharmacist, but it still produced an early flip.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester...
tips_feedback.why: We hanged Bob on a Sheriff Evil check without weighing that a Jester also reads Evil. The Jester revenge then killed a random Guilty voter (it happened to hit Peggy, a Yakuza, so we got lucky).

tips_feedback.tip: Unclaimed players, stay unclaimed / Don't hint at a power role on Day 1
tips_feedback.why: Olivia (Vigilante) stayed hidden and survived. Withholding role names kept the Katana focused on known investigators.

tips_feedback.tip: A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's block log, confirmed by Olivia's N3 block, made the block/no-kill pattern trustworthy and led to the correct Heidi hang.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's Not Evil on Heidi was correctly discounted, so the town didn't clear the actual Katana holder.

lessons.tip: Once a Lookout or Tracker has placed your Katana holder on the victim, move the Katana that same night to a member with no public trail. Keeping it on the exposed player marks them as the blocker's and the SK's obvious target, and leaves the team's best cover sitting on a player who is likely to die.

When a Party Animal claims and lays out their block log, kill them with the Katana next. Every block that lines up with a no-kill night becomes hang evidence against the lone holder, and town treats those matches as verified as soon as one block target confirms being blocked.

Spend the rig early, on any Day with a plausible town mislynch. A Clerk whose holder is exposed or who might take an SK hit can die with the token unused, and then it is worth nothing. One rigged Day 3 hang of a muddy claimant would have been worth more than waiting for a perfect setup.

Pool exact-role draws in night chat. If a Diviner or Surveyor group already drew 'Jester' and an Evil-checked player sits in that group, the Jester is probably that player. In that case, expect revenge on a random Guilty voter: think about how many teammates are exposed, and remember that a puppet or other next-Day effect lapses if its user dies (R21).

As the last Yakuza facing a known blocker, a skipped or blocked night points straight at whoever the blocker visited. Claim a role early with an alibi that fits, rather than staying unclaimed and claiming Vanilla only when cornered. A late Vanilla claim from the last unclaimed players is exactly where town looks.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't PM teammates by day, especially on Day 1. A visible PM triangle becomes the town's case all game.
tips_feedback.why: No Yakuza-to-Yakuza PMs ever showed up, so town had no cluster to build on. The only Day 1 PM pair (Niaj and Bob) led to the Jester, not to us.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory had no visiting role, so the Lookout's report of Mallory and Judy on Dave pointed straight at her. The tip should add: move the Katana as soon as the holder is seen.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester (pushes hard, self-nominates, seems eager to be tried) or an Executioner.
tips_feedback.why: Town ignored it and hanged Jester Bob 13-0, but the revenge happened to kill Puppeteer Peggy. That also voided her Day 3 puppet of Judy, which made the Yakuza fall apart quickly.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's caveat stopped her Not Evil check on Heidi from clearing her, and town hanged Heidi on Ivan's block/no-kill pattern instead.

lessons.tip: When a non-teammate reads Evil to a Sheriff, he is a Jester or Executioner. If the hang is already certain without you, vote Innocent on him. Every Yakuza Guilty vote is another ticket in the Divine revenge lottery, and that lottery killed our Puppeteer.

Don't spend the N1 block on whoever PMed you on Day 1; a prober is often a Jester fishing for attention. Block a likely investigator who could check the Katana holder, or a quiet organizer. Your block is wasted if it lands on a role with no night action.

Once a Party Animal claims and posts his block targets, kill him with the Katana at once. Every block he lands on the holder produces a 'block plus no kill' pattern that the town treats as proof. A lone holder can't afford to be blocked even once.

Don't all write identical fake Vanilla wills. After the first Yakuza flips with a fake Vanilla will, every later Vanilla claim or will looks the same. Vary the covers between teammates, or pick tokenless power roles that can't be checked.

Share Diviner results in a way that reaches every teammate before the Day votes. Our Diviner drew 'Jester' in Bob's group on N1, which meant Bob could be safely abandoned with Innocent votes and should never be blocked or targeted.

tips_feedback.tip: Do the vote math in night chat. If a teammate is doomed, bus them (Yes and Guilty)... Lone futile No or Innocent votes hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: We applied 'join the bandwagon' reflexively on Bob, who wasn't a teammate and was a likely Jester. All four of us voted Guilty, and the Jester's revenge killed Peggy. Innocent votes on a non-teammate Jester would have been safe and would have cut our revenge risk.

tips_feedback.tip: Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed (Vigilante).
tips_feedback.why: Olivia never named her role. Carol hid her exact token count, so the Yakuza never targeted her and she survived to the end.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester... If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored this and hanged Jester Bob 13-0, handing Bob his win. They got lucky when the revenge hit a Yakuza; the tip was right.

lessons.tip: Holding all tokens every night forfeits value. Once a mechanical lead exists (e.g. a Party Animal's block coincides with a no-kill night, or a late unclaimed Vanilla claim), fire a cheap Basic shot. If the shot is wasted, one token is a small loss, and it can end the game a day earlier.

When a claimed blocker's target lines up with a no-kill night and that pattern has already matched a flipped Yakuza once, treat it as a strong lead. Also verify the blocker independently: being blocked yourself and confirming it publicly is a cheap, solid confirmation.

A late Vanilla claim from a player who stayed unclaimed and echoed others while asking investigators for claims is the classic hiding spot for the last Yakuza. Do slot math on the flipped Yakuza roles (Pharmacist, Clerk, Puppeteer) to see which Yakuza roles could still be unaccounted for.

After a Jester hang, the revenge hits a random Guilty voter. Before a near-unanimous Guilty on a weakly verified Evil read, consider that the Sheriff reads the Jester and Executioner as Evil. Keep Guilty votes near a bare majority unless the claim is checked (e.g. 0 tokens alone doesn't rule out a Jester).
Short, results-first messages work. Most decisive days here took one or two messages per player, so bank budget early for trial days.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at a power role on Day 1 / stay unclaimed as Vigilante (Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed)
tips_feedback.why: Staying unclaimed kept me off the Katana list all game. The only cost was a Party Animal block on me, which I then used to verify Ivan publicly.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh who benefits: a Jester pushes hard and seems eager to be tried; keep Guilty votes to a bare majority
tips_feedback.why: We ignored it on Bob. The Sheriff's Evil read was actually a Jester, all 13 voted Guilty and gave him the win, and the revenge was a lottery (it luckily hit Puppeteer Peggy).

tips_feedback.tip: Sheriff: Jester and Executioner read Evil; post Not Evil with the Katana-holder caveat
tips_feedback.why: Grace posting her checks with caveats kept the town from over-clearing Heidi on her Not Evil read, which let Ivan's block lead carry the hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Don't PM teammates by day
tips_feedback.why: The only Day 1 PM pair was Bob (Jester) and Niaj (Pharmacist). Niaj's PM with a neutral nearly became a case on its own, which shows how visible any day PM is.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Shoot only on a mechanical lead
tips_feedback.why: It stopped me from shooting Judy, whose Trapper claim I had been suspicious of, so I avoided a misfire. In hindsight I could also have shot Heidi on N4 on Ivan's lead.

lessons.tip: Once a Lookout publicly names your Katana holder as a visitor to the Katana victim, move the Katana that night to an unexposed member. A Party Animal or Vigilante will target the named visitor, and the holder's Not Evil reading doesn't help if they're blocked or shot first.

Combine your exact-role draws with public Sheriff results. If a Diviner or Surveyor draws Jester in a group and a Sheriff then reads a group member Evil when they aren't your teammate, that player is almost surely the Jester. Every Guilty voter then risks the Divine revenge, so weigh it before piling on.

Day effects that need you to act lapse if you die that night (R21). Don't spend the token on a night when you face an elevated death risk, such as after voting Guilty on a likely Jester. Use it early when it can swing a trial, rather than hoarding it until the team is thin.
Spend one-shot tokens (Clerk rig, puppet) while the team still has numbers. Our Clerk died holding an unused rig after waiting for a 'perfect' mislynch day that never came.

As the last Yakuza facing a claimed blocker whose block lined up with a past no-kill night, a skipped or blocked night will be pinned on you. Claim something with a night action early, and set up an alternative suspect before the blocker names you, not during your trial.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to the member whose role matters least and who has no reason to visit.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory (Clerk) had no visiting role, so when the Lookout saw her at Dave's she had no cover. Keeping the Katana on her N2 let Ivan's block stop the kill.

tips_feedback.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates.
tips_feedback.why: Town hanged Bob purely on his lone D1 PM to Niaj plus an Evil check. He was the Jester, and his revenge killed me, the Yakuza Puppeteer.

tips_feedback.tip: A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's verified N3 block on Olivia plus two block/no-kill nights became the mechanical case that hanged Heidi, the last Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Sheriff: Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's immediate D2 claim and Evil result on Bob anchored the town and made her credible for the rest of the game.

lessons.tip: Don't kill Yakuza early. Every Yakuza you remove makes the Village stronger and leaves you alone against a large town. Target Village power roles (blockers, Sheriff, Accountant) and let the Yakuza thin the town for you. Only turn on the Yakuza once the town is small.

Don't attack the player the Yakuza obviously want dead, such as a Lookout who just exposed their Katana holder. A double kill wastes your night, and the 'Katana and Serial Killer' cause confirms you are still active. Pick a target the Katana is unlikely to hit.

An early Vanilla claim is the natural hiding spot for an SK, and any Oracle or exact-role checker will test Vanilla claimers once SK kills are public. Stay unclaimed longer, or claim a role that fits your 0 tokens and that some flip or result appears to back up. Don't volunteer Vanilla on Day 2.

Arguing 'that claim is uncheckable, test it first' fails against a claim the flip will confirm or break. The town reasons that a fake claim would hang its claimant tomorrow, so they hang you now. A better defense is a concrete counter-mechanic, such as another player's result that contradicts the claim.
A publicly announced Trapper trap works as a deterrent. Killers will avoid the trapped player, so treat that player as protected, and expect kills to land elsewhere.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them
tips_feedback.why: It helped the town against me. Erin's Oracle guessed 'Serial Killer' on my unverifiable Vanilla claim and got me hanged on Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's investigation or protection target, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: Judy publicly announced her trap on Grace, and it scared me off ever attacking Grace. Announcing a Trapper's trap protects the target, so the tip doesn't fit Trappers.

tips_feedback.tip: If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it and hanged Jester Bob 13-0. The revenge happened to hit Yakuza Peggy, but with 13 Guilty voters the town was mostly gambling on its own members.

tips_feedback.tip: A power claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia confirmed she was blocked on Night 3, as Ivan had announced the day before. That verified Ivan, and his block/no-kill pattern hanged the last Yakuza, Heidi.

summary: The Village won because three night-time disruptions broke the Yakuza: the Serial Killer, a Party Animal and a lucky Jester revenge. On N1 Rupert (Serial Killer) killed Niaj (Pharmacist), while the Katana killed Dave (Medic). On D2 the town hanged Bob 13-0. Bob was a Jester: Grace's Evil check plus his lone D1 PM to Niaj looked damning, but the Evil read also fit a Jester, as did Carol's 0-token audit. Bob's revenge happened to hit Peggy (Puppeteer), which also wasted her puppet on Judy. Alice's Lookout result (Judy and Mallory visited Dave) exposed Mallory. On N2 Ivan (Party Animal) blocked her, stopping the Katana, and the SK killed her that same night. Heidi inherited the Katana and killed Alice on N3, alongside the SK. Heidi then went after Erin instead of the blocker. On D4 Erin's correct Oracle guess got Rupert hanged. On N4 Ivan blocked Heidi and there was no kill. That gave the town a second block/no-kill match; Olivia had confirmed the N3 block was real, so the town trusted Ivan's log. Heidi, a late Vanilla claimant, was hanged on D5. Yakuza mistakes: they all voted Guilty on a likely Jester even though Heidi's divine had drawn Jester from Bob's group. They kept the Katana on a holder the Lookout had exposed. The lone survivor never targeted Ivan, the blocker.

lessons.tip: An Evil Sheriff result on a player with 0 tokens and no night results fits a Jester or Executioner as well as Yakuza. Before hanging, ask who benefits. If you still hang, keep Guilty votes near a bare majority so the Jester's revenge has fewer town targets.
lessons.evidence: Bob read Evil and audited 0 tokens. He never pushed for his own hang, yet the town voted 13-0 Guilty and he flipped Jester. The revenge happened to land on Peggy (Yakuza), but it could just as easily have killed a power role.

lessons.tip: If your own information suggests the nominee is a Jester, don't all pile onto Guilty. One or two Innocent votes look fine once a Jester flips, and each Guilty vote is a ticket in the revenge draw. Share that information in night or day planning.
lessons.evidence: Heidi's N1 divine on Bob's group (Bob/Carol/Dave) drew Jester. All three surviving Yakuza still voted Guilty on Bob, and the revenge killed Peggy along with her unused-in-play puppet.

lessons.tip: Once a Lookout publicly names your Katana holder as a visitor to the victim, move the Katana to an unexposed teammate. Expect blockers and killers to target the exposed holder; reading Not Evil to the Sheriff doesn't protect against a block.
lessons.evidence: After Alice named Mallory, the Yakuza kept the Katana on her so she would read Not Evil. Ivan blocked her on N2, which stopped the kill on Alice, and the SK killed her that night.

lessons.tip: When a claimed role-blocker's log keeps lining up with your no-kill nights, kill the blocker first. Every night they live, they either stop your kill or build a block/no-kill pattern against you.
lessons.evidence: Ivan claimed Party Animal on D3 and had already stopped Mallory. Heidi attacked Alice on N3, who died to the SK anyway, and then Erin on N4. Ivan blocked Heidi on N4, and that no-kill night got her hanged.

lessons.tip: A blocker should hit the most suspected possible Katana holder each night and publish the full log. Two blocks followed by a night with no kill, confirmed by a blocked player, make a strong mechanical case.
lessons.evidence: Ivan blocked Mallory on N2 and Heidi on N4, and neither night had a Katana kill. Olivia confirmed she was blocked on N3, so the town trusted Ivan's log over Heidi's 'second Pharmacist' defense.

lessons.tip: Spend guesses on roles that matter if right, such as Serial Killer on an unverifiable Vanilla claimant, rather than repeatedly guessing Grunt on players likely to be another Yakuza role.
lessons.evidence: Erin wasted N1 and N2 on 'Grunt' guesses (Bob was a Jester, Mallory a Clerk). On N3, Erin guessed Serial Killer for Rupert, who had claimed Vanilla early. It was right and led to his hanging.

lessons.tip: Don't volunteer a Vanilla claim early when nobody has pressed you. An unprompted, uncheckable Vanilla claim becomes a natural target for exact-role checks.
lessons.evidence: Rupert claimed Vanilla on D2 during Bob's trial without being asked. Erin later said she guessed him as SK because 'the SK had to be hiding behind' an unverifiable Vanilla claim.

lessons.tip: A day PM between two players proves nothing about alignment until both have flipped. Don't treat 'PM'd a flipped Yakuza' as confirmation of anything.
lessons.evidence: The town's whole case against Bob rested on his D1 PM to Niaj, and Bob was a Jester, not a teammate.

tips_feedback.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. Players who DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new info are a likely Yakuza bloc.
tips_feedback.why: The town treated Bob's lone D1 PM to Niaj as proof that Bob was Yakuza and hanged a Jester. The revenge only helped the town by luck.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask who benefits: a Jester or an Executioner. If you must hang one, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: This was ignored on D2: 13 Guilty votes on a 0-token, Evil-reading Jester. Following it would have avoided giving the revenge 12 possible targets among the other voters. It landed on Yakuza Peggy only by chance.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. If a trusted Lookout names X as the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof.
tips_feedback.why: Alice's N1 result exposed Mallory. Ivan blocked her on N2, stopping the Katana kill on Alice, and Mallory flipped Clerk.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool even after the Yakuza die. Not Evil and Vanilla claims don't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: Erin targeted Rupert's unverifiable Vanilla claim with a Serial Killer guess on N3, confirmed it, and the SK was hanged on D4.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Post every Not Evil with that caveat.
tips_feedback.why: Grace attached this caveat to her N4 Not Evil on Heidi. As a result nobody treated it as clearing Heidi, and she was hanged as the Katana holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Shoot only on a mechanical lead, never on a mismatch alone, since a Cardinal misfire kills twice. Use Basic shots and stay unclaimed.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia held all her shots and stayed unclaimed. No town player was shot, and the Cardinal Frank never died, so no extra Good player was killed.

issues.description: Night 1: Ivan (Party Animal) and Niaj (Pharmacist) both role-blocked Bob (Jester, no night action). R9 says 'Role-blocked players are told they were role-blocked' but also 'blocking a player who has no night action has no effect'. The moderator read 'no effect' as including no notice and didn't tell Bob. The night checker read it the other way and flagged it as an error. The rule should say clearly whether players with no night action are notified. The moderator was also inconsistent: on N3, Olivia was told she was role-blocked even though she chose not to act.

Under the night checker's (and the instructions') reading of R9, the moderator wrongly withheld the role-block notice from Bob on Night 1. This hid information a player was entitled to: Bob could have used 'I was blocked N1' in his Day 2 play.

Night 2: the moderator spent Peggy's puppet token twice: once through the puppet op and again with a manual set_tokens. The harness logged a warning and clamped the count to 0. There was no in-game effect because Peggy had exactly one token, but it is a double-spend pattern to avoid.

Night 2: the Katana passed from the dead Mallory to Heidi, and the Yakuza night report went to both Heidi and Peggy, before Bob's Jester revenge was applied ('left to code'); the revenge then killed Peggy that same night. R8 says the Katana passes to a random living Yakuza after that night's results, so Peggy should have been excluded. This time it landed on Heidi, but the ordering means the Katana could have been given to a player who was dying that night.

Night 3: Judy (Trapper) didn't act because the rules don't say whether placing a trap again on the already-trapped player resets the 'armed from the next night on' delay. The Trapper text should say whether re-placing on the same target keeps the trap armed.

Day 5: Carol argued that since the Pharmacist died N1, 'only a real Party Animal could have blocked Olivia' N3, treating Ivan as confirmed. This ignores the rule that roles can repeat and the role list isn't public. Grace corrected it. Similarly on Day 2, Grace asserted that Bob 'is not an Ex-Con or Jester, he's Yakuza', which an Evil Sheriff result plus a PM cannot establish.

Yakuza players (Heidi, and Peggy's feedback) found there is no chance to communicate between night results and the start of Day. This makes coordination that depends on night results, such as Diviner info feeding a Puppeteer's scripted messages, impossible. The players had to invent in-message signal words. It would help to state this limitation explicitly in the Yakuza prompt.
